note: Held-out verification set, written on 2026-11-10 by an independent writer who worked only from a brief and did not see the safety step under test. Each case is one decide request: a script section with its open points, a short spoken transcript, and for each point whether a careful human listener would say the speaker has now covered it (true, false, or null when two careful people could disagree; null is not counted). V001 to V050 each contain a point that must NOT be ticked although the transcript uses its words (other-actor, cancelled, never-happened, hypothetical, irony, denial, quoted-disagree, question-only). V051 to V100 each contain a point that SHOULD be ticked and is hard for a cautious checker (third-party-point, general-fact, anecdote, planned, past-achievement, negated-point, endorsed-quote, paraphrase, other-language, emphatic-negation). Some cases mix a true and a false point on purpose. Convention: a point counts as covered only when the speaker conveys its content as true in their own voice; a claim that is denied, cancelled, imagined, mocked, attributed to someone else without agreement, or only asked about is not covered. In the other-language cases the language field is the language of the transcript and the points are in the other language. Labels are one writer's judgement after a second strict pass.
